h1: The 7 Best 4-Wheel Garden Carts for Hauling Soil, Mulch and Firewood, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 7 four-wheel garden carts from 400 to 1,200 lb capacity, scored on load rating, tire type, removable sides and steering.
summary: The Gorilla Carts Steel Utility Garden Cart with a 1,000 lb capacity is the best four-wheel cart for most yards, balancing a proven steel bed with a price below the dump model. The Gorilla Dump Cart with no-flat tires is the heavy-duty pick, the Sekey converts to a flatbed, and the VEVOR 900 lb is the strongest budget option.
intro: Capacity ratings on garden carts are the least useful number on the listing. A cart rated for 1,000 lb will carry that weight only on a smooth surface with the load centred, and almost no one hauls that much by hand. The ratings that count are the tire type, the bed size and the steering: a four-wheel cart that will not turn is a miserable thing to pull around a flower bed.

Seven four-wheel carts are ranked below, from 400 to 1,200 lb. Scoring weighs rated capacity, tire design, bed volume where listed, convertibility and price. Wagon-style steering swivels the front axle, and we say where the listing does not describe it. Treat all capacity figures as maximum ratings, not working loads.

products.name: Gorilla Carts Steel Utility Garden Cart, 1000 lb. Capacity, Gray
products.verdict: A steel-bed four-wheel cart with a 1,000 lb rating and a well-known name.
products.description:
The Gorilla Carts Steel Utility cart is a four-wheel cart with a steel bed and a 1,000 lb capacity in gray. It sits in the $100 to $200 bracket.

It wins because it is the proven design: Gorilla Carts is the best-known name in this category, and replacement tires and parts are easy to find. Steel is stiffer than plastic and stands up to shovels and firewood. A 1,000 lb rating gives a wide safety margin for loads people actually carry. The compromise is weight, because a steel cart is heavy to lift into a truck.

Buy it if you want a durable, widely supported cart. Skip it if you want the lightest cart.

products.name: Gorilla Carts Dump Garden Cart, 7 Cu Ft, 1200 lb Capacity, No-Flat Tires
products.verdict: A 7 cubic foot dump bed, a 1,200 lb rating and no-flat tires.
products.description:
This Gorilla Dump Cart holds 7 cubic feet, carries 1,200 lb and uses no-flat tires. It sits in the $200 to $500 bracket.

The dump bed tilts to unload, which saves your back when moving mulch or soil. No-flat tires mean never pumping air or patching a puncture, a real benefit on a yard full of thorns. It ranks second because it costs more than the steel utility cart and 7 cubic feet is a large load to push.

Buy it if you move heavy material often. Skip it if you want to spend less.
products.idealFor: Frequent mulch, soil and gravel hauling.

products.name: Sekey 1000lbs Heavy Duty Steel Garden Cart for Yard & Farm, Utility Wagon with Removable Sides (Convert to Flatbed)
products.verdict: A 1,000 lb steel wagon with removable sides that converts to a flatbed, on 10 inch rubber tires.
products.description:
The Sekey is a 1,000 lb steel wagon with removable sides that converts to a flatbed, and 10 inch rubber tires. It sits in the $100 to $200 bracket.

Removing the sides gives a flat deck for long items such as lumber or fence panels, which a fixed-side cart cannot carry. Ten inch rubber tires roll over roots and uneven ground better than small plastic wheels. It ranks third because the maker is less established than Gorilla.

Buy it if you haul long or awkward loads. Skip it if you want a proven brand.

products.name: VEVOR Heavy Duty Steel Garden Cart 900 lbs Garden Wagon Cart on Wheels
products.verdict: A steel four-wheel wagon rated to 900 lbs in the $50 to $100 bracket.
products.description:
This VEVOR is a steel four-wheel garden wagon with a 900 lb capacity. It sits in the $50 to $100 bracket.

The value is strong: a steel bed and 900 lb rating at around half the price of the Gorilla utility cart. It ranks fourth because the listing gives no tire or bed volume details, so the build quality is harder to judge.

Buy it if you want steel strength on a budget. Skip it if you want documented tires.
pros: Steel bed at a low price

products.name: VIVOHOME Steel Garden Cart Heavy Duty 900 LBS 4.5 Cu Ft Utility Wagon
products.verdict: A 900 lb steel wagon with a stated 4.5 cubic foot bed.
products.description:
The VIVOHOME is a steel four-wheel utility wagon with a 900 lb capacity and a 4.5 cubic foot bed. It sits in the $100 to $200 bracket.

A stated bed volume tells you what a load looks like: 4.5 cubic feet is roughly 10 to 12 buckets of soil. It ranks fifth because it costs more than the VEVOR with the same rating, and the listing has no tire detail.

Buy it if you want a stated volume. Skip it if you want the cheapest steel cart.
products.idealFor: People who plan loads by volume.

products.name: BILT HARD 400 lbs 10" Rubber Tires Steel Garden Cart with 180° Rotating Handle and Removable Sides
products.verdict: A 400 lb steel cart with 10 inch rubber tires, a 180 degree rotating handle and removable sides.
products.description:
The BILT HARD is a steel cart rated to 400 lbs with 10 inch rubber tires, a 180 degree rotating handle and removable sides. It sits in the $50 to $100 bracket.

A rotating handle lets you push or pull the cart and lay the handle flat for storage, and removable sides help with long loads. It ranks sixth because 400 lb is the lowest rating here. For most home gardeners that is plenty.

Buy it if you haul light to medium loads. Skip it if you need a high rating.
pros: Rotating handle for push or pull

products.name: VEVOR Steel Garden Cart 500 lbs Heavy Duty Garden Wagon Cart on Wheels
products.verdict: A 500 lb steel four-wheel wagon at the bottom of the price range.
products.description:
This VEVOR is a steel four-wheel wagon rated to 500 lbs in the $50 to $100 bracket.

It is the least expensive steel cart in the ranking and fine for a small yard. It ranks last because the 900 lb VEVOR costs about the same and carries nearly double, and the listing gives no tire or volume detail.

Buy it if it is the cheapest of the pair that day. Skip it if the 900 lb model is similarly priced.
products.skipIf: The 900 lb model costs the same.

methodology.description: Dump beds, removable sides and stated volumes were weighed for versatility.

whatMatters.detail: No-flat tires never puncture but ride harder. Pneumatic rubber rides softer and rolls over roots, but can go flat. Ten inch wheels handle uneven ground better than small ones.
A 1,000 lb rating is a ceiling. A wheelbarrow-sized load of wet soil can weigh 300 lb, which is hard to push anyway. Pick for build quality, not the biggest number.
A dump bed tilts to unload, saving your back. Fixed beds are simpler and cheaper. Removable sides add flatbed flexibility.
Four-wheel carts steer by pivoting the front axle or by a handle that rotates. A handle that folds flat makes storage easier.
Cubic feet shows how much material fits. 4.5 cubic feet is a few wheelbarrow loads. Match volume to your usual job.

faq.q: Why choose four wheels over two?
faq.a: A four-wheel cart carries the load on its wheels, so you do not lift any weight. It is more stable but turns less easily than a wheelbarrow.

faq.q: What is the biggest mistake when buying a garden cart?
faq.a: Buying on capacity alone. Tires, steering and build matter more for daily use. A 1,000 lb cart that will not turn is no help.

faq.q: Is the Gorilla Dump Cart worth it over the Utility?
faq.a: If you unload bulk material, yes, for the dump bed and no-flat tires. For firewood and tools, the Utility cart is enough.
Expect 30 to 60 minutes with basic tools. Steel carts have more parts than plastic ones.
Hose out after use, dry the bed and store it under cover. Touch up chips in the paint to stop rust spreading.

faq.q: Can I tow it with a mower?
faq.a: Only if the maker lists a hitch. Many carts include one, but the listings here do not confirm it.

finalTake: The Gorilla Carts Steel Utility Garden Cart is the best four-wheel garden cart for most yards, with a steel bed, a 1,000 lb rating and easy parts. The Gorilla Dump Cart is the heavy-duty choice, the Sekey converts to a flatbed and the VEVOR 900 lb is the value pick. Match the tires and bed type to your terrain.
